summary: A coherent, correctly-assembled Victorian lamp with a good silhouette (stepped finial, cross-mullioned lantern, brass collar accents, believable dark-iron-plus-brass palette) — clearly above programmer art. But it sits at 'competent', not 'good': the column is a smooth spindly pole with no visible fluting, the base is a flat placeholder-style slab instead of a moulded plinth, and the lantern glaz

defects.fix: Thicken the column from its current ~0.6-stud pole profile to ~1.2 studs at the base tapering to ~0.9 under the collar, and shorten it by ~2-3 studs so the lantern sits closer to the classic 1:1 ratio with the shaft. Right now it reads as a
defects.observed: The column is a long thin smooth pole carrying an oversized lantern. In all three views the shaft reads as spindly relative to the lantern head and the wide base plate — real Victorian lamp columns are chunkier, roughly a third of the head

defects.fix: Replace the flat plate with a 3-tier moulded plinth: a 6.5-stud square step ~0.4 studs tall, a 5-stud step ~0.6 studs tall, then a chamfered 3.5-stud cap block ~1.2 studs tall before the column starts. Add a 0.3-stud torus-style ring where列
defects.observed: The base is a single wide flat slab — a beveled square plate sitting directly on the ground with a small gold fitting at its centre. It reads as a placeholder pad, not a cast-iron plinth. A Victorian base needs stepped/moulded tiers

defects.fix: Add 6-8 shallow vertical fluting strips (0.15-stud half-round cylinders) around the lower two-thirds of the shaft, and give the existing collar a second, wider ring 0.5 studs below it so the transition has a moulded profile instead of one
defects.observed: The brief asked for a fluted column. At this camera distance the shaft reads as a smooth untextured cylinder — no flutes, no taper steps, no ring detail along its length. The single gold collar band is the only ornament on ~12 studs of

defects.fix: Inset the glass panes 0.2 studs behind the mullion frame and add a 0.15-stud inner sill at the bottom of each face so the glazing has visible depth from oblique angles
defects.observed: The lantern glass is a flat glowing plane flush with the mullion frame — there is no visible recess or pane depth, so the housing reads as a decal on a box rather than a glazed lantern
